questions.question: What is AlgoBlocks?
options: A text-based programming language for advanced developers
A visual, block-based learning platform for understanding algorithmic logic
A database management tool for storing algorithms
A hardware simulation tool for testing processors
questions.explanation: AlgoBlocks is a visual, block-based educational platform designed to teach algorithmic logic and complexity analysis to beginner students.

questions.question: How are programs constructed in a block-based system?
options: By writing text code in a terminal window
By dragging and connecting pre-built logical blocks that represent programming constructs
By drawing diagrams on a whiteboard
By configuring settings in a menu-driven interface
questions.explanation: In a block-based system, programs are built by dragging and snapping together visual blocks that each represent a programming construct such as variables, loops, or conditions.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Workspace Canvas?
options: To display execution output and error messages
To store saved projects in the cloud
To serve as the main area where blocks are arranged and connected to define program logic
To visualize memory usage during program execution
questions.explanation: The Workspace Canvas is the central area where learners drag and connect blocks to design and build their algorithmic programs.

questions.question: What does the Output Console display?
options: The Big-O complexity rating of the algorithm
The Python source code generated from blocks
The results of program execution, including printed values and errors
The memory usage graph over time
questions.explanation: The Output Console shows the results of running the program, including any printed output, return values, and runtime errors.

questions.question: What does sequential execution mean?
options: Instructions are executed in a random order determined by the CPU
Instructions execute only when a condition is true
Instructions are executed from top to bottom in the order they appear
Instructions run in parallel across multiple threads
questions.explanation: Sequential execution means each instruction runs one after another from top to bottom, following the natural order they appear in the program.

questions.question: What is a variable used for?
options: To define a reusable block of code that can be called multiple times
To store and manage a named piece of data that can change during execution
To loop through a list of items automatically
To compare two values and branch the program flow
questions.explanation: A variable is a named storage location that holds a value which can be read, modified, and reused throughout the program.

questions.question: What programming construct is used for iteration?
options: A conditional (if/else) statement
A function definition
A variable assignment
A loop (for or while)
questions.explanation: Loops (for or while) are the constructs used for iteration, allowing a set of instructions to repeat multiple times.

questions.question: What is conditional logic?
options: Logic that executes the same path regardless of input
Logic that determines which branch of code executes based on whether a condition is true or false
Logic that runs only once at program startup
Logic used exclusively inside loops
questions.explanation: Conditional logic (if/else) directs program flow by evaluating a condition and executing different blocks of code depending on whether the result is true or false.

questions.question: What is an array?
options: A single variable that stores one value at a time
A function that processes numbers sequentially
An ordered collection of elements stored under a single variable name, accessible by index
A loop that iterates a fixed number of times
questions.explanation: An array is a data structure that stores multiple values in an ordered sequence, where each element is accessible by its index position.

questions.question: What does the Complexity Analyzer evaluate?
options: The visual appearance of the block arrangement
The number of variables used in the program
The time and space complexity of each line of code
The network speed required to run the program
questions.explanation: The Complexity Analyzer evaluates each line or block of code and assigns a time and space complexity rating, helping learners identify performance bottlenecks.

questions.question: What represents constant time complexity?
options: O(n) — performance scales linearly with input size
O(log n) — performance scales logarithmically
O(n²) — performance scales quadratically
O(1) — performance does not change regardless of input size
questions.explanation: O(1) means the operation always takes the same amount of time regardless of how large the input is.

questions.question: What represents linear time complexity?
options: O(1) — constant regardless of input
O(n) — performance grows directly proportional to input size
O(n²) — performance grows quadratically
O(log n) — performance grows logarithmically
questions.explanation: O(n) means the number of operations grows linearly as the input size increases — doubling the input roughly doubles the execution time.

questions.question: What does the Memory Visualizer track?
options: The Big-O time complexity of each block
The network bandwidth consumed during execution
Changes in variable states, array contents, and the call stack over the course of execution
The number of blocks used in the workspace
questions.explanation: The Memory Visualizer shows how variable values change, how arrays are modified, and how the call stack grows and shrinks during program execution.

questions.question: What is a function call stack?
options: A list of all variables declared in the program
A data structure that records the active function calls, tracking which function called which and in what order
A log of all output printed to the console
A visual timeline of loop iterations
questions.explanation: The call stack is a LIFO data structure that keeps track of all active function calls during execution, including where each function was called from.

questions.question: Why is code execution considered dynamic rather than static?
options: Because the code is written using drag-and-drop blocks
Because the program structure is fixed and never changes
Because the actual behavior, variable values, and execution paths are determined at runtime based on input and state
Because execution speed depends on the programming language chosen
questions.explanation: Execution is dynamic because the actual values, paths taken through conditionals, and number of iterations are only determined when the program runs with real input data.
